solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Most of the fault lies in this economy

indicators.note: 'Most of' THE keeps all but its last letter

blocks.note: THE without its final E
a rift is a geological fault

explanation.surface: Someone blaming the economy for the whole mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The fault' reads as one phrase, but it splits: 'Most of the' is TH, and the fault is a rift in the rock.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: thrift is the careful spending that economy also names.

clue.text: The graduate a short time in charge of certain subject

blocks.note: used as printed
MA = Master of Arts, a graduate
T is the abbreviation for time
IC = in charge

explanation.surface: A new graduate briefly put in charge of teaching a subject.
explanation.walkthrough: IC for 'in charge' is a standard crossword abbreviation, as is MA for a graduate.
explanation.definitionFit: Thematic means relating to a particular subject or theme.

clue.text: Having basic education in odd places, not so well done

indicators.note: the three Rs sit in the first, third and fifth squares, with the other letters slotted between them

blocks.note: the three Rs: reading, writing and arithmetic
no word in the clue really supplies A and E; the setter leaves the even squares to the definition and the crossing letters, so this block only fills the gap

explanation.surface: A cook with a patchy schooling who undercooks the meat.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'three Rs' is a British phrase for basic schooling: reading, writing and arithmetic. Put an R in each odd-numbered square; the clue is loose, since nothing clues the A and E between them, and the definition has to finish the job.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain comparative: steak cooked less is rarer, so 'not so well done' is the same idea said negatively.

clue.text: Warm coat, in that situation, cut in advance

indicators.note: THERE is cut short, losing its last letter

blocks.note: a fur is a warm coat
THERE ('in that situation') without its final E

explanation.surface: A warm coat, tailored in advance for some chilly situation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' looks like tailoring the coat; it trims THERE instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean additionally or beyond, as in 'further to my letter' and 'paid in advance'.

clue.text: Blood type different? That’s a nuisance

blocks.note: B is a blood group
other = different

explanation.surface: A hospital mix-up over a patient's blood type causes a headache.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blood type' tempts O or AB; only B leaves room for OTHER.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, both nouns for something that annoys.

clue.text: For example, general proposal covering one chapter

blocks.note: an offer is a proposal
Roman numeral one
C = chapter

explanation.surface: A general proposal that happens to include a chapter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'General proposal' reads as a vague suggestion; 'general' actually belongs to the definition, the rank.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a general is one rank of commissioned officer, signalled by 'For example'.

clue.text: Followers creating aggravation between husband and child

indicators.note: 'between husband and child' puts the aggravation in the middle of the other two pieces

blocks.note: H = husband
anger = aggravation
a son is a child

explanation.surface: A family row where the trouble sits between father and child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Aggravation' here is plain annoyance, not a worsening; H for husband is a register abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Hangers-on are followers who attach themselves to someone.

clue.text: Take part in quarrel I should enjoy

indicators.note: the answer is a part taken from inside the next words

blocks.note: the answer runs across the last three letters of the first word, all of I and the first two of the third

explanation.surface: Someone who admits they would love to join a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take part in' sounds like joining the quarrel; it is telling you to take part of the words.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both verbs mean to take pleasure in.

clue.text: Sign of grief, having broken up or parted

indicators.note: the letters of OR PARTED are broken up and reset

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters

explanation.surface: Tears after a couple has broken up or separated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broken up' fits the heartbreak story perfectly, which is how it hides its job.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: one drop of a tear is the classic outward sign of grief.

clue.text: Rewrote as script in adaptation for RADA, perhaps

indicators.note: an adaptation rearranges its source, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 11 letters

explanation.surface: A drama school rewriting a text as a script.
explanation.walkthrough: RADA is the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art in London; 'perhaps' looks like a hedge but is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To paraphrase is to rewrite in other words.

clue.text: Penalty to pay, about a pound in the end

blocks.note: a fine is a penalty paid
used as printed
L = pound (libra)

explanation.surface: Paying a fine of about a pound in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like 'roughly'; it means FINE wraps around A and L.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the finale is the closing part of a show or piece of music.

clue.text: Hot gaseous mixture — that may end in a bang

definitions.text: that may end in a bang

blocks.note: H = hot, as on a tap
air is a mixture of gases

explanation.surface: A hot explosive gas mixture that may go off with a bang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bang' sounds explosive, fitting the gas; but bangs is the American word for a fringe, cut straight across the forehead.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair cut short at the front ends in a bang, or fringe.

clue.text: Bad luck, having set mousetrap, for example

blocks.note: set hard, like jelly or concrete
Mousetrap is a British brand of cheddar cheese

explanation.surface: Tough luck for the mouse once the trap is set.
explanation.walkthrough: The mousetrap sounds like the device; it is the cheese. 'Hard cheese' is British slang for bad luck, often said without sympathy.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Hard cheese!' is a British expression meaning bad luck.

clue.text: Two sprinters involved in cool events?

indicators.note: the letters are involved, i.e. tangled up together

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 12 letters

explanation.surface: Two runners taking part in some trendy races.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cool' reads as trendy; it means literally cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Winter sports are events held in cold conditions.

clue.text: Instant idea underlying the Web, primarily

indicators.note: take the primary, first, letters of 'the Web'

blocks.note: first letters of The and Web
an inkling is a vague idea

explanation.surface: A flash of inspiration that lies behind the World Wide Web.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'underlying' means placed below, so the idea is written after the Web's initials. 'Primarily' covers both words.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: 'in the twinkling of an eye' means instantly, so the noun alone stands for an instant.

clue.text: Storyteller held up in act, no longer on track

indicators.note: in a down clue, held up means turned to read upwards

blocks.note: a liar tells stories
a deed is an act

explanation.surface: A storyteller delayed in the middle of a performance, losing the thread.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'storyteller' is a liar, the crossword's favourite fib.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a derailed train has come off the rails, and figuratively a derailed plan has gone off course.

clue.text: Switched dancing there as redirected

indicators.note: the letters are sent off in new directions

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 12 letters

explanation.surface: Dancers swapping places when the choreography changes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dancing' looks like the anagram signal, but it is fodder; 'redirected' does that job.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean swapped one for another.

clue.text: Tastiest extremity on swine?

blocks.note: the surface asks for the best bit; really it is the pig's foot, cooked as a dish
the extremity is on the animal: its foot

explanation.walkthrough: A pig's foot, eaten as a delicacy in Britain, is the tasty extremity of the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The foot of a pig is its trotter, boiled or roasted as a dish.

clue.text: That man’s right account of what happened

blocks.note: his = that man's
a Tory is a British Conservative, on the political right

explanation.surface: Someone insisting their version of events is the correct one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right' reads as correct; it is the political right, a Tory being a member of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a history is a record or narrative of past events.

clue.text: State of a canal — on your head be it

blocks.note: a Central American country, named for the canal that cuts through it
a straw hat, worn on the head

explanation.walkthrough: 'On your head be it' is an idiom for taking the blame, but read literally it describes a Panama hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Panama is the country with the canal, and a panama is a straw hat.

clue.text: They bear heavy burdens, so include supporting frames in case?

blocks.note: to pack something is to include it in a case
horses are supporting frames, like a clothes horse or sawhorse

explanation.surface: Packing the frames into a case for animals that carry heavy loads.
explanation.walkthrough: The horses here are frames, as in a clothes horse; 'pack … in case' spells out what PACK means.
explanation.definitionFit: Packhorses are animals that carry heavy loads.

clue.text: Like some Asians, that is, endlessly getting together

indicators.note: both THAT and IS lose their last letters
the two shortened words are joined

blocks.note: THAT without its end
IS without its end

explanation.surface: Asians who, endlessly sociable, keep getting together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That is' tempts IE, but each word is docked separately.
explanation.definitionFit: Thai describes people from Thailand, some Asians.

clue.text: Row across British or Italian river

blocks.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
B = British

explanation.surface: Rowing across a British or an Italian river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' tempts the boating sense; it is a row of seats, a tier.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tiber is the river that flows through Rome.

clue.text: Convert to aims of a revolutionary leader

indicators.note: the letters are converted into a new form

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 6 letters

explanation.surface: Converting people to a revolutionary leader's aims.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Convert' reads as winning followers, which suits the leader; it rearranges TO AIMS.
explanation.definitionFit: Maoist means of or following Mao Zedong, the revolutionary leader.

clue.text: It indicates you’ve arrived — don’t knock it!

definitions.text: It indicates you’ve arrived — don’t knock it!

blocks.note: a device that announces a visitor
the surface reads 'don't criticise it'; really, ring instead of knocking

explanation.walkthrough: 'Don't knock it' means don't criticise it, but a visitor with a doorbell literally need not knock.
explanation.definitionFit: A doorbell announces a caller at the door.

clue.text: Woollen cloth that’s good in short jacket

indicators.note: ANORAK is cut short, losing its last letter

blocks.note: G = good
ANORAK, a hooded waterproof jacket, without its K

explanation.surface: Recommending a woollen cloth for a short jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short jacket' suggests a cropped style; it is an anorak with its tail cut.
explanation.definitionFit: Angora is a soft woollen cloth made from goat or rabbit hair.

clue.text: Cross section of lengthy bridge

indicators.note: the answer is a section cut from the next words

blocks.note: the answer spans the last two letters of the first word and the first four of the second

explanation.surface: An engineering drawing: a cross section of a long bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross section' is one technical phrase in the surface; split it, and 'Cross' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A hybrid is a cross between two breeds or kinds.
